title: 1. Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
objective: Study-guide review — ICCS423 v2 — L11: Web Security 2 (XSS · CSRF · Files · SSRF · API · Proactive Controls): 1. Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).

items: Attacker injects malicious JavaScript into a page that the victim's browser executes in the trusted context of the target site
Impact: session theft, keylogging, redirect to phishing, defacement, drive-by malware

blocks.text: XSS is "injection into the browser" — converts the user-site trust relationship into attacker control.

rows: Client-side JS reads from URL fragment / postMessage
Crafted-link clickers; server never sees payload

items: Context-aware output encoding — HTML body, attributes, JS string, URL, CSS each need different encoding
Content Security Policy (CSP) — script-src 'self' 'nonce-xyz'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'
HttpOnly cookies — limits damage even if XSS lands
Use safe APIs — textContent over innerHTML; React JSX auto-escapes (avoid the dangerous-set-inner-HTML escape hatch)
Sanitization library for user-supplied HTML — DOMPurify (client) / Bleach (Python)

blocks.text:
``python # HTML context — Jinja escapes by default from markupsafe import escape return f"

Hello {escape(name)}

" ``
Real-world: British Airways (2018) — Magecart script injection on payment page → 500K cards → £20M GDPR fine. Subresource Integrity (SRI) + strict CSP would have blocked the skimmer.
